reason: Half the census is right and everything built on it fails. Driven at 1440 and 390 across all twelve states, indigo paints exactly two objects on owner-flight, owner-editing, phone and desk (.b-todayRule and the lead .b-tick), one on day (.b-dayNow border-top), one on print (the lead tick), and none on publish, unfurl, ended, owner-empty or either loading state. That much holds. The argument does not. (1) It reopens the lock. lock.md's mechanical section reads 'it is the today rule and the filled tick on the next thing, and nothing else', and the supersedes table ratifies it as Stands; the finding deletes one of the two named uses and adds a third the lock excludes by name. That is a founder-level decision, not a seat's refinement. (2) The measurement carrying the whole force of the argument is wrong. The two accents are not '130px apart on the phone': in the phone state they are 311px apart at both 390 and inside the 1440 frame, and on owner-flight at 390 they are 367px apart. At 1440 they are in different columns entirely (rule x186-530, tick x682) with a gutter between them. 127px is the gap round-4 measured between .b-todayLabel and .b-origin - a different pair of objects. (3) The publish half of the fix is a literal no-op. .b-linkField computes border-width 0px and border-style none; the 1px fore-16 border on the publish link belongs to .b-linkRow. `.b-linkField { border-color: var(--accent) }` paints nothing at all. (4) Where it would paint, it would be worse: b.css:31 sets --focus: var(--accent) in the paper room, so a permanent indigo edge on the one screen whose primary control is a focusable link field plus a Copy button wears the focus hue permanently. (5) 'Nothing is lost' is false. Demote .b-todayRule to --fore-16 and it becomes byte-identical to the generic hairline already used for .b-linkRow's border and the same-day stack divider - the exact 'reads as a divider rather than as today' failure a prior round corrected by clamping it from 1068px to 344px. Round-4 refuted deleting .b-todayLabel on the ground that it is 'the only payoff for .b-todayRule'; round-2's sharpened fix deliberately held the rail origin mark at fore-28 'so the indigo horizon rule stays the only accented statement of today'. This inverts both. (6) The 'unspent accent is wasted accent' premise contradicts a ruling the panel already made: round-4 accepted that a day with no live item shows no indigo at all, 'since nothing is happening and there is nothing to mark'. Publish, unfurl and ended are handovers, not moments on the measure. The residue - that LANGUAGE.md says 'spent once per screen' while four surfaces carry two marks - is a wording question about whether the rule counts objects or ideas (today is the measure's origin and the lead tick is its nearest point ahead: two ends of one now), and if it is ever settled it is settled in the document, not by repainting a locked accent.
sharpenedFix: None. If the LANGUAGE.md line is to be reconciled at all, change the sentence to say the accent marks the measure's now - its origin and its next - once each and nowhere else, which is what the artifact, the lock and the day-state fix already do. Do not touch .b-todayRule, and do not put indigo on publish.
